question: Across measurement sources, consider only source-years with a known source year, a non-null measurement value, a known allele class, and at least two measurements. For each source, take the two source-years with the highest measurement counts, breaking ties by choosing the more recent year, compute the difference between the average measurement value in the selected latest year and the selected previous year, and then report the overall average of those per-source changes, rounded to two decimal places.
gold_sql:
WITH source_year_stats AS (
    SELECT
        apm.measurement_source_id,
        ms.source_year,
        COUNT(*) AS measurement_count,
        AVG(apm.measurement_value) AS avg_measurement_value
    FROM allele_peptide_measurements AS apm
    JOIN measurement_sources AS ms
        ON apm.measurement_source_id = ms.source_id
    JOIN alleles AS a
        ON apm.allele_id = a.allele_id
    WHERE apm.measurement_value IS NOT NULL
      AND ms.source_year IS NOT NULL
      AND a.class IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY apm.measurement_source_id, ms.source_year
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
),
ranked_years AS (
    SELECT
        measurement_source_id,
        source_year,
        measurement_count,
        avg_measurement_value,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY measurement_source_id
            ORDER BY measurement_count DESC, source_year DESC
        ) AS year_rank
    FROM source_year_stats
),
surviving_years AS (
    SELECT
        measurement_source_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN year_rank = 1 THEN source_year END) AS latest_selected_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN year_rank = 2 THEN source_year END) AS previous_selected_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN year_rank = 1 THEN avg_measurement_value END) AS latest_avg_measurement_value,
        MAX(CASE WHEN year_rank = 2 THEN avg_measurement_value END) AS previous_avg_measurement_value
    FROM ranked_years
    WHERE year_rank <= 2
    GROUP BY measurement_source_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 2
)
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(latest_avg_measurement_value - previous_avg_measurement_value), 2) AS average_change_between_periods
FROM surviving_years

question: Across all publicly accessible digital outputs that have an active metadata entry indicating a source, what is the average number of active visualizations per output? Count visualizations at the output level, and average those counts over all outputs that meet both conditions.
gold_sql:
WITH qualified_outputs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT do.output_id
    FROM digital_outputs AS do
    JOIN output_metadata AS om
      ON do.output_id = om.output_id
    WHERE do.is_public = 1
      AND om.is_active = 1
      AND om.metadata_key = 'source'
),
visualization_counts AS (
    SELECT qo.output_id,
           COUNT(dv.vis_id) AS visualization_count
    FROM qualified_outputs AS qo
    LEFT JOIN data_visualizations AS dv
      ON qo.output_id = dv.output_id
     AND dv.is_active = 1
    GROUP BY qo.output_id
)
SELECT AVG(visualization_count) AS avg_visualizations_per_qualified_output
FROM visualization_counts

question: For every article that has at least one access event with a recorded access date, provide an access-activity summary along with its journal. Return the article ID, article title, journal ID, journal title, earliest access date, latest access date, the number of days between those two dates, total access events, number of unique users, number of unique IP addresses, average accesses per day computed as total access events divided by access span plus one day, the share of access events tied to a known user account, the ratio of unique IP addresses to total access events, the average length of the recorded access-type text, the maximum IP-address string length, and an activity label of high_activity for at least 100 events, medium_activity for 25–99 events, and low_activity otherwise. Order the results by longest access span first, then by highest total access events.
gold_sql:
WITH article_access_stats AS (
    SELECT
        a.article_id,
        a.title AS article_title,
        j.journal_id,
        j.title AS journal_title,
        MIN(al.access_date) AS first_access_date,
        MAX(al.access_date) AS last_access_date,
        CAST(julianday(MAX(al.access_date)) - julianday(MIN(al.access_date)) AS INTEGER) AS access_span_days,
        COUNT(al.access_id) AS total_access_events,
        COUNT(DISTINCT al.user_id) AS distinct_users,
        COUNT(DISTINCT al.ip_address) AS distinct_ip_addresses,
        AVG(CASE WHEN al.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS known_user_ratio,
        AVG(CASE WHEN al.access_type IS NOT NULL THEN LENGTH(al.access_type) END) AS avg_access_type_length,
        MAX(LENGTH(COALESCE(al.ip_address, ''))) AS max_ip_address_length,
        CASE
            WHEN COUNT(al.access_id) >= 100 THEN 'high_activity'
            WHEN COUNT(al.access_id) >= 25 THEN 'medium_activity'
            ELSE 'low_activity'
        END AS activity_label
    FROM articles AS a
    JOIN journals AS j
        ON a.journal_id = j.journal_id
    JOIN access_logs AS al
        ON al.article_id = a.article_id
    WHERE al.access_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
        a.article_id,
        a.title,
        j.journal_id,
        j.title
)
SELECT
    article_id,
    article_title,
    journal_id,
    journal_title,
    first_access_date,
    last_access_date,
    access_span_days,
    total_access_events,
    distinct_users,
    distinct_ip_addresses,
    ROUND(
        1.0 * total_access_events / NULLIF(access_span_days + 1, 0),
        2
    ) AS accesses_per_day,
    ROUND(known_user_ratio, 3) AS known_user_ratio,
    ROUND(
        1.0 * distinct_ip_addresses / NULLIF(total_access_events, 0),
        3
    ) AS ip_diversity_ratio,
    ROUND(avg_access_type_length, 2) AS avg_access_type_length,
    max_ip_address_length,
    activity_label
FROM article_access_stats
ORDER BY access_span_days DESC, total_access_events DESC
